evidence.paraphrase: At the beginning of his seventh year, Vināyaka bathes and performs daily rites. Crowned, lion-mounted, he bears goad, axe, lotus and fear-removing noose; staff/skin, gold jewelled earrings, waterpot, darbha, yellow silk, musk mark, crescent, pearl necklace and serpent at navel adorn him. Playful roar shakes heaven/earth; cātaka birds mistake thunder, rivers leap; Aditi and Kaśyapa rejoice and praise their ancestry’s fortune.

evidence.paraphrase: Unnamed Kāśī king visits Kaśyapa, exchanges embraces/bows, receives seat and six-taste meal. Kaśyapa asks why king has neglected his purohita. King apologizes for royal preoccupation and personally requests performance of his son’s wedding. Kaśyapa declines because observing Cāturmāsya, offers capable son. King accepts; father sends Vināyaka despite separation sorrow; child bows parents and boards king’s chariot.

evidence.paraphrase: Aditi tells king her child must be guarded constantly, since upheavals occur wherever he is; guard like eyelids the pupil, and return as received. King agrees, bows and departs with child by swift chariot into great forest.

evidence.paraphrase: Forest belongs to Dhūmrākṣa, strong brother of Raudraketu and paternal uncle of Narāntaka. For10000years he worships thousand-rayed Sun, hanging feet from tree with head down and drinking smoke; requests supreme all-destroying weapon and subjection of three worlds. After long time Sun sends an unfailing radiant weapon toward the ascetic.

evidence.paraphrase: Vināyaka sees sky-filling brilliance, flies and catches weapon. King marvels and reflects that gain/loss/life depend on destiny. To ascertain its power child weighs/tosses weapon upwards; it falls roaring on Dhūmrākṣa, splitting him in two. Falling pieces crush rocks/trees and cover500bow-lengths of ground.

evidence.paraphrase: Dhūmrākṣa’s sons Jaghana and Manu attend their father, see his destruction, rush angrily and accuse king of bringing child to kill him. They say father formerly protected king from Narāntaka. King fears loss of kingdom, swears by brāhmaṇa/Īśvara that purohita’s son was brought only for wedding, asks no obstruction and offers child to them. Vināyaka protests handing a bound child to enemies, asks what king will tell parents and warns angry Kaśyapa could burn king.

evidence.paraphrase: Sons approach to devour him; child roars, shakes three worlds and breath propels them to cloud layer. After two muhūrtas Jaghana and Manu fall in Narāntaka’s city crushing houses. Amid commotion messengers inspect apparently dead sons, find both conscious, revive/attend them and hear their account: father killed by Kaśyapa’s son, selves thrown by breath, child travelling with Kāśī king. Messengers report to Narāntaka.

evidence.paraphrase: Pataṅga and Vidhula approach as mighty whirlwinds. Dust obscures world, houses/trees fall, garments/turbans fly, frail people fall. King rejoices, leaves chariot, bows and praises deeds beyond ordinary boy, cosmic creator with innumerable manifestations beyond fleshly sight.

narrative_events.details: Seventh-year daily rites, lion and four weapons/ascetic ornaments; playful cosmic roar delights parents.

King receives hospitality and requests purohita for son’s wedding; Cāturmāsya prevents Kaśyapa travelling. Son substituted, bows parents, boards chariot; Aditi requires constant care and safe return, king agrees.
Narrative flashback identifies paternal uncle/brother,10000-year inverted smoky Sun tapas, weapon and dominion request. Sun sends unfailing radiant weapon; dominion not explicitly granted.
Child flies, intercepts weapon and tosses to test power; fall splits Dhūmrākṣa, fragments crush surrounding rocks/trees500bow-lengths. King wonders at destiny.
Sons accuse king of killing their father/protector. Afraid of Narāntaka king asserts wedding purpose and offers child. Child protests breach of parental trust and warns Kaśyapa’s anger.
Roar/breath launches attacking sons; after two muhūrtas they fall into Narāntaka city crushing homes. Messengers discover both alive and transmit their report.
1000rākṣasas ordered to capture child/kill if fighting. Roar kills some; others injured, including arrow-torn bellies, flee and report.
Survivors warn child unbeatable; Narāntaka ridicules warning, equips host and orders plunder/distraction or killing king and child. Commander threatens any disobedient demon.
City reception and sixteen-offering worship; eager women seek sight, one barred woman dies while meditating. Four social groups perceive varied forms according to disposition.
Child knowingly counters malicious play-embrace by crushing both demons; ten-yojana corpses and divine flower/praise follow.
Whirlwinds devastate city and lift chariot; child immobilizes chariot, grabs topknots, whirls and kills both. King bows recognizing divine creator and countless forms.
Axe splits disguised stone100ways; child fists emerging terrifying demon down after onlookers flee.
King seats, worships, feeds child/friends and prepares night bed after sandhyā; four guards stationed while king/queen retire by child’s leave.
